result.summary: The landlord approved a leak repair at 16 Brindlewick Mews, but it has stopped. The contractor saw an unidentified fibrous ceiling lining (possibly asbestos, not confirmed) where he needed to cut. A young child lives in the flat. The landlord's approval covers the plumbing only, and she wants the cost and timing before agreeing to a specialist check. Nobody has priced one yet. I escalated to a human at high priority so staff can get a surveyor quote and take it to the landlord. I moved the ticket on to landlord_approval, placed a 2-day hold, updated the tenant with safety advice and recorded the key facts.
result.situation: A compression joint above the kitchen ceiling leaks whenever the kitchen tap is used. Kellan Orve (Mossbarrow Pipe Services) can't reach it through the hatch. Making the approved ceiling opening would mean cutting near a pale, fibrous-looking lining that nobody has identified. There is no material survey (asbestos check) on file. The work stopped and nothing was disturbed. The tenant has stopped using the tap. The landlord has declined to cover anything beyond the plumbing until she knows the cost and timing.

escalation.reason: A suspected hazardous ceiling lining blocks the approved leak repair. The specialist assessment needed is outside the landlord's approval and has no price. A young child lives in the flat.
escalation.handover_summary: The leaking joint can only be reached by cutting near an unidentified fibrous lining, so the work stopped and nothing was disturbed. The tenant has stopped using the kitchen tap. The landlord's approval covers the plumbing only, and she wants the cost and timing before agreeing to more. The plumbing estimate amount isn't visible in the CRM. The CRM contractor record shows the building manager instead of Kellan Orve.
escalation.recommendation: Get a quote and earliest date for an asbestos survey or sample from a licensed or UKAS-accredited firm. Ask Bren Talwick (building manager) whether the block has an asbestos register. Take the cost and timing to Ossa Fenlow for approval. Ask Kellan whether the pipe can be isolated meanwhile without disturbing the ceiling. Fix the CRM contractor record.

judgement.why_this_decision: There is a possible hazardous material in a home with a young child (event 17), and the leak keeps coming back (event 20). The landlord has said her approval doesn't cover an assessment and asked for cost and timing first (event 22). Nobody can give that cost yet: Kellan can't price it (event 23). Getting a specialist quote and judging the safety risk needs agency staff, so I escalated at high priority. The stage was behind the evidence, so I moved it to landlord_approval. The tenant was told what to do next and when they'll hear from us.
